# Parser regression fixtures

Every source record remains in the parser result so consuming apps can reject the whole input. Invalid cells are null; no valid subset is silently fitted. cases.json specifies exact retained rows. Its historical refused field (and the browser -refused.csv export) lists the row indices of new refusal diagnostics, not removed records. Existing missing int/float and not int/float warnings keep their original text and are not included in that list.

Semicolon/tab separators accept decimal commas in float columns. Quoted decimal commas in comma-separated input invalidate the affected cell. Excess fields make column boundaries ambiguous: retain the label and null all declared numeric fields, with a row/column warning and corrective advice. Short rows retain null trailing optional numeric fields. Missing required columns are explicitly null; existing empty numeric cells use the original coercion diagnostics.

Undeclared OR/RR/HR plus CI input is refused without conversion: retain the record, null ratio/CI and declared numeric fields, and request explicit log-effects and SEs. Fully declared ratio/CI schemas parse unchanged. CI text in SE cells and commas in int columns invalidate only that cell. Integer diagnostics quote the original input. Numeric study labels remain strings. n/N/sd/sample size never fuzzy-map to se/sei/vi/variance; se/sei never fuzzy-map to variance.

The original 40 fixtures retain their controls and now assert the revised record-retention contract. Eight missing-TP/FN/FP/TN fixtures cover empty and whitespace-only cells followed by a valid record; dta-control verifies complete counts. Unit tests additionally pin missing/malformed float warning strings and simultaneous invalid cells. No contract spec or tolerance was changed.

parser.html loads only the shared parser. Each Playwright case removes stale exports before navigation, asserts exact rows and diagnostics, and exports the page callback's numeric values (including TP/FN/FP/TN). R independently reads those same source fixtures using base read.csv/read.csv2, compares every retained row, exact labels and refusal indices, and numeric values at 1e-9. A deliberately wrong value must be rejected before R_CHECK_PASS can print. schema.csv records the caller's declared columns; rules.csv records separators. No page output is synthesized outside Playwright.

The R projection also preserves unmatched exported source fields: guard-se retains the text "12" under se while vi remains missing. Regression assertions reject both losing that field and assigning it to variance; variance-control verifies the declared numeric path. Existing fixture expectations and the 1e-9 tolerance are unchanged.

Round-3 alias regression: se-to-sei and sei-to-se failed against the pre-fix parser; sei-exact-control passed. Standard-error aliases remain compatible in both directions, while n/N/sd/sample size and variance guards remain unchanged. The GOSH-shaped malformed float retains its exact legacy warning. Page exports now include sei, and R independently applies only these two equivalent-name aliases when no exact header claims the destination; numeric comparisons remain at 1e-9.
